paragraphs: I've worked in Moraga long enough to know that the cul-de-sac end of Brookfield Drive in Camino Woods is one of those addresses that doesn't come up often, and when it does, people pay attention. A fully reimagined 1964 home with a Viking and Miele kitchen, a renovated primary suite, and that kind of privacy and setting at the quiet end of the street  -  that's a combination that genuinely stands out. So when the listing came off the market after 28 days without a sale, I took notice, and that's why I'm writing.

Twenty-eight days is short enough that it doesn't leave a stain, but it does raise a question worth asking honestly: why didn't it connect? The home itself isn't the issue. The renovation quality, the location, the floor plan  -  the fundamentals are strong. What I saw in the listing strategy was a gap between what this home actually offers and how that story reached buyers. The description led with exclamation points and kitchen appliance brands, but it never built the case for why $761 per square foot in Moraga is the right number for this specific property. Buyers at this price point compare carefully, and they needed more than appliance names to feel confident about the value.

I've put together a short analysis of the three key friction points I think held this listing back, along with a clear picture of how a different approach could change the outcome. It's not a pitch, it's a diagnosis  -  with a specific plan attached.

If you're already working with a real estate agent toward a new listing, please feel free to set this aside  -  no hard feelings at all. If you're not, I'd welcome a short conversation whenever the timing feels right. There's no pressure and no obligation, just an honest look at what I think is possible here.

exec_summary.headline: A Fully Reimagined Camino Woods Home  -  and a Listing That Never Made the Case for It
exec_summary.p1: 102 Brookfield Drive has the ingredients Lamorinda buyers at this price point are actively searching for: a quiet cul-de-sac setting in one of Moraga's most established neighborhoods, a thoughtfully renovated interior with professional-grade appliances, updated baths, and new windows and lighting throughout. At 2,358 square feet on a nearly 10,000-square-foot lot, with four bedrooms and a renovated primary suite, this home checks the boxes that move buyers off the fence. The bones are solid, the finishes are current, and the location is genuinely desirable.
exec_summary.p2: The listing history doesn't match those fundamentals. Twenty-eight days on the market and no sale isn't a verdict on the home  -  it's a signal that the marketing strategy didn't do the work of connecting this property's specific assets to the buyers most likely to value them. The listing description named the appliances and called it a chef's kitchen, but it never answered the question every serious buyer is quietly asking: why is this home worth $1,795,000 compared to what else I could buy in Moraga right now? Without that narrative, price-conscious buyers move on before they ever request a showing.
exec_summary.p3: A relaunch here needs to do one thing above all else: build the visual and narrative case that the renovation quality, the cul-de-sac privacy, and the Camino Woods setting together justify the number. Buyers who find that case compelling will move quickly on a home like this.

forensics.title: Friction #1: The Listing Description Sold Appliances, Not a Home
forensics.body: The MLS remarks for 102 Brookfield opened with 'Stop the search  -  this is the one you've been waiting for,' which is the kind of phrase buyers have read a thousand times and learned to skip past. What followed was a list of features rather than a narrative: Viking and Miele appliances, LED canned lighting, replacement windows. None of that is wrong, but none of it is a story. A buyer comparing this home to others in the $1.7M range in Moraga isn't looking for a list of what was replaced. They want to understand what it feels like to live here, why the cul-de-sac end of Brookfield is different from a mid-block lot, and what makes the renovation quality worth the premium. That story was never told, and without it, the listing read like a form submission at a price point that demanded something more.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork's Zillow Showcase placement pairs a professionally written narrative with enhanced listing pages where all buyer inquiries route back to our team, not to random third-party agents who don't know the home.

forensics.title: Friction #2: Premium Pricing Without a Visual Proof Strategy
forensics.body: At $761 per square foot, 102 Brookfield is priced in the upper tier of the Moraga renovated range, and that's defensible given the scope of the updates, the lot size, and the cul-de-sac position. But 'defensible' and 'understood' are two different things. Buyers at this price point are comparing against other well-renovated homes, and they make quick judgments based on what they see online before they ever schedule a showing. Standard MLS photography shows rooms. It doesn't convey the privacy of a cul-de-sac setting, the scale of the lot relative to the street, or the way natural light moves through a home with all-new windows. Without visual proof that matches the price, the number feels like an ask rather than an answer.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: A Sky Tour gives buyers an aerial view of the lot position, the cul-de-sac setting, and the street presence that ground photography simply can't replicate, and it's one of the first things that makes a $761-per-square-foot number feel earned before anyone walks through the door.

forensics.title: Friction #3: The Right Buyers Were Never Actively Reached
forensics.body: In the current rate environment, buyers in the $1.7M to $1.8M range in Moraga are a well-defined group: typically relocating professionals from San Francisco or Oakland, often with school-age children, researching Lamorinda neighborhoods months before they're ready to move. These buyers don't browse Moraga listings passively  -  they're comparison-shopping across multiple cities and price points, and they need to find a home like 102 Brookfield while they're still forming their shortlist. A standard MLS distribution puts the listing in front of whoever happens to be searching that day. It doesn't find the buyer who is three weeks from being ready and doesn't yet know Camino Woods exists.

positioning_table.verdict: At $761/sqft versus a benchmark range of $700-$750/sqft, this home sits near the upper end of that range. At $761 per square foot, 102 Brookfield sits at the upper end of Moraga's premium tier. The renovation scope, cul-de-sac lot, and professional-grade kitchen all support that positioning  -  but the listing strategy never built the case for it in a way that gave buyers the confidence to act at that number. The right marketing approach doesn't lower the price; it closes the gap between what this home is worth and what buyers understood about it.

pillars.title: Pillar I  -  Telling the Camino Woods Story, Not Just Listing the Address
pillars.body: The cul-de-sac end of Brookfield Drive is a meaningfully different proposition than a standard Moraga street, and buyers who have never driven it don't know that yet. A relaunch built around this home starts with that setting: the privacy, the safety, the neighborhood character that Camino Woods has maintained for decades. BrightWork's 3D Matterport tour lets buyers experience the interior layout from anywhere, at any time, so by the time they request a showing, they already feel like they know the home.

pillars.title: Pillar II  -  Making $761 Per Square Foot the Obvious Conclusion
pillars.body: At $1,795,000, buyers are doing math in their heads the moment they see the price. The renovation scope at 102 Brookfield supports that number, but supporting it and proving it are different things. A targeted campaign that isolates the specific upgrades  -  the professional-grade appliances, the refreshed baths, the new windows and lighting  -  and frames them against what buyers typically find at this price point in Moraga turns a question into an answer. That's the work the first listing didn't finish.

pillars.title: Pillar III  -  Finding the Buyer Before They Find Someone Else
pillars.body: The buyer for this home almost certainly exists in the SF and East Bay relocation pipeline right now. They have children, they care about schools, and they are comparing Lamorinda against other options without a strong picture yet of what Moraga specifically offers.
